@Zachery Sutton @Laura Lopez 

It's a bit difficult for me to follow this figma because the structure is a bit implicit and I think we are missing some dimensions.

Can we structure this a bit more so that it's more clear to see the differences?

My suggestion would be:
1. Align on either dark mode or light mode. Suggest light mode.
2. Display the "offer mask" UI, and the modal to the right of it, using the LTR flow that we are all used to, and helping us ensure terminology consistency.
3. Separate logged-in vs non-logged in (as you do)
4. Show the control and the variants (right now this is a bit confusing because the control is (partly) on the right hand side and the variants are all on the left side)
5. For the logged-in case, separate first time use ("create an email mask") vs ongoing use ("use an email mask")
6. For the offer mask, in all cases, show the "when ask to save passwords is enabled" and "when ask to save passwords is not enabled", in both the short term version (where we have to live with the current styling for "save passwords) and long term version (where we don't).

Apologies that this is a lot, but I have a feeling that this will clarify the situation for everybody.
@Laura Lopez If we are saying "create" in the prompt, shouldn't the modal also say "create"?
@Zachery Sutton @Laura Lopez Notice that these icon is different from that of the variant above. Was that intentional and part of the test?
@Zachery Sutton Note that we have a little key here, but we don't have it in the others. Is that intentional? (fwiw, I like the little key you added)

@Zachery Sutton @Laura Lopez
What if we had a different icon, separating the first-time use vs ongoing? e.g. this same email but with a "plus" sign, since it's about adding/creating a new mask?

@Zachery Sutton Can we separate the short-term, where "manage passwords" will be styled like it is now? vs the long term one, where it's styled as we want?

This is important for the product review as we want to show both, acknowledging we are going out with a less than ideal one (but better than the current one)

This is super cool but technically hard. The code only sees the values like "etsy.com" or the full page title like "Etsy - shop for handmade, vintage, custom and unique gifts for everyone". It's quite hard to condense the website text in a way we know will fit well with the rest of the text.
Next? Let's go?

Can likely just say forwards here

Masked email = not a term ppl are familiar with

Look at the onboarding email to make sure it aligns
CTR is high!

We don't show a user's previous masks unless they're using the extension
@Laura Lopez I moved your design notes over too. I may have pulled the wrong ones over...if so my bad!!!
Suggestion: How about "First, sign up or log in to your Mozilla Account to create your first email mask".
Shouldn't this say "Create email mask"? Or if we want "Use", I suggest we change the language immediately above to say "By using an email mask, you agree..."

"protect against spam" is not spelling out what is being protected.

How about "Protect yourself from spam" or "Protect your inbox from spam"? (or "against", idk).
"to your account" --> "to your Mozilla Account", might be good to say here, because I could imagine somebody thinking they are going to sign up or log in to their email account.

@Laura Lopez I don't have a suggestion here but "masked emails" is not quite accurate and somebody who doesn't get it intuitively might not get it. Its "emails sent to your masked address". But that's too long?
Can we pull just the domain name, no link?

Wonder if we can just pull the site name instead of using it as a link? 

Firefox will forward masked emails from Etsy to laura@gmail.com.

@Zachery Sutton can we do a smaller treatment for these so it's seen more as legalese? 

Also... are links blue or just underlined?
I think I missed it somewhere, what's under this expansion?
Wonder if its worth saying "Firefox will" so that users more directly tie this to the browser
Wondering if it's possible / we have precedent for treating this more like a disclaimer so it doesn't have so much weight.

I loathe the sign up or sign in. I've seen it "Sign up/in" other places but I think that guidance Katie linked to is probably good. Something like 85% of users don't have an account, and an even smaller minority percentage of those have an account but are logged out. If we want to make the case that we can say just sign up, that's great. Though I am curious if Emily's study tested sign up vs. sign in and sign in won!
Are you planning on user testing? I'd be curious if you need the "First sign up or" line here, since the next thing they see will introduce the idea of an account.
These options feel kind of link-ey. Too many paths out - on error pages we bold the url to set it off as variable without making it actionable. Maybe that's worth it here too.

I like including the domain. Admittedly, I don't know much about masks. Let's assume etsy sells my masked email to a data broker, and they try emailing me from a non-etsy domain. Do those not get forwarded? @Laura Lopez
Did you consider "Create email mask"? Feels more indicative of what's happening, use could imply there's something that exists already.
I kind of want this to be formatted as a question vs. a directive. I think i'd also prefer to have the value prop in here, something like "Protect against spam with an email mask"
@Laura Lopez - Digging this one
@Laura Lopez - This one sounds too overpromising IMO. Makes me think my email could never be hacked into, yadda yadda.

@Laura Lopez - The forwarding bit feels a bit functional. I wonder if there's a way to position this more benefit forward - or in more plain language. 

Riffs...

You’ll still receive emails from Amazon in your regular inbox, with your address is masked.

Emails from Amazon will still come to your inbox, but with your email masked.

@Laura Lopez - Emily shared with me that, for mobile onboarding, an onborading card that simply used "Sign in" in the CTA performed better than one that addressed both scenarios - Sign in or sign up. Of course, not sure if that can be applied directly here, but it's an interesting input to consider... and I'd be inclined to at least make the button one action - maybe Sign up to match the header? And the body still references both?

@Laura Lopez - The construction here, to lead with a link to a potentially 'unknown' thing / term, throws me a little bit. Wdyt about...

Protect against spam by hiding your real email address with an _email mask_.
Next screen doesn't actually say "Create an account to use an email mask" -> possibly in the future but rn it's general ("Create an account")
CTA -> sign up or sign into your account

We know what domain the user is on so could call that out here

Helps with the qualification of the protection
The place where someone is logging in = may be construed as a spammer (which isn't necessarily true!)
Do not mention Firefox in accounts
